ཐམས་ཅད་དག །འཁོར་ལོའི་ཚུལ་རྣམས་རབ་ཏུ་བསྐོར་བ་ཡི། །དེ་དག་གི་ཡང་གསུང་དབྱངས་མི་ཟད་ལ། །བློ་ཡི་སྟོབས་ཀྱིས་བདག་ཀྱང་རབ་ཏུ་འཇུག །མ་འོངས་བསྐལ་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་འཇུག་པར་ཡང་། །སྐད་ཅིག་གཅིག་གིས་བདག་ཀྱང་འཇུག་པར་བགྱི། །
གང་ཡང་བསྐལ་པ་དུས་གསུམ་ཚད་དེ་དག །སྐད་ཅིག་ཆ་ཤས་ཀྱིས་ནི་ཞུགས་པར་སྤྱད། །དུས་གསུམ་གཤེགས་པ་མི་ཡི་སེང་གེ་གང་། །དེ་དག་སྐད་ཅིག་གཅིག་ལ་བདག་གིས་བལྟ། །རྟག་ཏུ་དེ་དག་གི་ནི་སྤྱོད་ཡུལ་ལ། །སྒྱུ་མར་གྱུར་པའི་རྣམ་ཐར་སྟོབས་ཀྱིས་འཇུག །གང་
ཡང་དུས་གསུམ་དག་གི་ཞིང་བཀོད་པ། །དེ་དག་རྡུལ་གཅིག་སྟེང་དུ་མངོན་པར་བསྒྲུབ། །དེ་ལྟར་མ་ལུས་ཕྱོགས་རྣམས་ཐམས་ཅད་དུ། །རྒྱལ་བ་དག་གི་ཞིང་རྣམས་བཀོད་ལ་འཇུག །གང་ཡང་མ་བྱོན་འཇིག་རྟེན་སྒྲོན་མ་རྣམས། །དེ་དག་རིམ་པར་འཚང་རྒྱ་འཁོར་ལོ་བསྐོར། །
མྱ་ངན་འདས་པ་རབ་ཏུ་ཞི་མཐའ་སྟོན། །མགོན་པོ་ཀུན་གྱི་དྲུང་དུ་བདག་མཆིའོ། །ཀུན་དུ་མྱུར་བའི་རྫུ་འཕྲུལ་སྟོབས་རྣམས་དང་། །ཀུན་ནས་སྒོ་ཡི་ཐེག་པའི་སྟོབས་དག་དང་། །ཀུན་ཏུ་ཡོན་ཏན་སྤྱོད་པའི་སྟོབས་རྣམས་དང་། །ཀུན་ཏུ་ཁྱབ་པ་བྱམས་པ་དག་གི་སྟོབས། །
ཀུན་ནས་དགེ་བའི་བསོད་ནམས་སྟོབས་དག་དང་། །ཆགས་པ་མེད་པར་གྱུར་པའི་ཡེ་ཤེས་སྟོབས། །ཤེས་རབ་ཐབས་དང་ཏིང་འཛིན་སྟོབས་དག་གིས། །བྱང་ཆུབ་སྟོབས་རྣམས་ཡང་དག་སྒྲུབ་པར་བྱེད། །ལས་ཀྱི་སྟོབས་རྣམས་ཡོངས་སུ་དག་བྱེད་ཅིང་། །ཉོན་མོངས་
སྟོབས་རྣམས་ཀུན་ཏུ་འཇོམས་པར་བྱེད། །བདུད་ཀྱི་སྟོབས་རྣམས་སྟོབས་མེད་རབ་བྱེད་ཅིང་། །བཟང་པོ་སྤྱོད་པའི་སྟོབས་ནི་རྫོགས་པར་བགྱི། །ཞིང་རྣམས་རྒྱ་མཚོ་རྣམ་པར་དག་བྱེད་ཅིང་། །སེམས་ཅན་རྒྱ་མཚོ་དག་ནི་རྣམ་པར་དགྲོལ། །ཆོས་རྣམས་རྒྱ་མཚོ་རབ་
ཏུ་མཐོང་བྱེད་ཅིང་། །ཡེ་ཤེས་རྒྱ་མཚོ་རབ་ཏུ་རྟོགས་པར་བྱེད། །སྤྱོད་པ་རྒྱ་མཚོ་རྣམ་པར་དག་བྱེད་ཅིང་། །སྨོན་ལམ་རྒྱ་མཚོ་ཡོངས་སུ་རྫོགས་པར་བྱེད། །སངས་རྒྱས་རྒྱ་མཚོ་རབ་ཏུ་མཆོད་བྱེད་ཅིང་། །བསྐལ་པ་རྒྱ་མཚོར་མི་སྐྱོ་སྤྱད་པར་བགྱི། །གང་ཡང་དུས་གསུམ་

...continually turn the wheels of the Dharma; I too shall engage with their inexhaustible melodic speech through the power of my intelligence.

I shall enter into all future eons in a single instant. I shall practice by entering into whatever the measure of eons in the three times may be in just a fraction of a moment.

I shall behold in a single instant those who are the Lions among Men who appear in the three times. I shall always enter their sphere of activity through the power of miraculous liberation.

Whatever arrays of realms exist in the three times, I shall manifest them upon a single atom. Thus, I shall engage in the array of the realms of the Victorious Ones in every direction without exception.

I shall go before all the Protectors—those Lamps of the World who are yet to come, who will sequentially attain Buddhahood, turn the wheel, and demonstrate the final peace of nirvana.

Through the power of swift miracles, the power of the vehicle that is the door to all things, the power of conduct possessing every virtue, and the power of all-pervading loving-kindness;

Through the power of all-encompassing merit and virtue, the power of wisdom free from attachment, and the powers of wisdom, skillful means, and meditative absorption, I shall perfectly accomplish the powers of Enlightenment.

Completely purifying the power of karma, totally destroying the power of mental afflictions, rendering the power of the <term>Maras</term> <gloss>demonic forces</gloss> powerless, I shall perfect the power of exceptionally good conduct.

Purifying oceans of realms, liberating oceans of sentient beings, seeing clearly oceans of phenomena, and realizing oceans of wisdom;

Purifying oceans of conduct, fulfilling oceans of prayers, making offerings to oceans of Buddhas, I shall practice without weariness for oceans of eons.

All those specific prayers for the conduct of Enlightenment...

# CHRY SIPPVS. LIB. VII.

<sig>Nu iij</sig>

Regarding the small speech to Stagoras, two; regarding speeches against propinations, and regarding those at rest to Onetor, two; regarding the covered <note>a reference to the "Sorites" or "Veiled" paradox</note> to Aristobulus, two; regarding the latent to Athenades, two. 

**Eighth composition.** Regarding the useful to Menecrates, eight; regarding speeches which consist of the infinite and defined, to Pasylus, two; regarding the useful speech to Epicrates, one. 

**Ninth construction.** Regarding sophisms to Heraclitus and Pollis, two; regarding ambiguous dialectical speeches to Dioscorides, five; against the art of Arcesilaus to Sphaerus, one. 

**Tenth construction.** Against custom to Metrodorus, six; regarding custom to Gorgippides, seven. 

Logical things which are outside the aforementioned four differences, and which contain logical questions sparingly, not connected and reduced into a body: the numbered questions are thirty-nine. All volumes of the logical part together are three hundred and eleven. 

**Ethical reason**, regarding the emendation of moral notions, first order.

english:
<meta>This page continues Giambattista della Porta’s 15th book of "Natural Magic," which focuses on the "hunting arts" (aucupium). While the previous page discussed using chemical mixtures and baits to catch fish, this page transitions into folk remedies and "magical" tricks for managing animals used in or encountered during the hunt, specifically dogs and birds of prey.</meta>

<page-num>543</page-num>
<header>ON FOWLING <note>original: "DE AVCVPIO," referring to the art of catching birds or hunting with them.</note></header>

...hairs, or holding dung, or those who have the vervain herb <note>original: "peristereon herbam," likely *Verbena officinalis*, a plant often associated with protection in folklore</note>. A black stone like a bean is found in the Nile; upon seeing it, dogs do not bark. You shall carry a dog's tongue <note>original: "linguam canis"; this may refer literally to the animal part or the plant Hound's-tongue (*Cynoglossum*)</note> placed in your shoe under your big toe, or if you carry a dried dog's heart with you, according to Sextus <note>Sextus Placitus, a 4th-century medical writer</note>; or hare's hair or dung, according to Pliny. Or you shall carry a cut-off tail of a young weasel on your foot, or give the dog a frog in a morsel of food; all these things are for evading the barking of dogs. Nigidius <note>Publius Nigidius Figulus, a Roman scholar and contemporary of Cicero known for his works on magic and nature</note> says that dogs flee the sight of one who pulls a tick from a pig and carries it for a little while. Oppianus <note>A 2nd-century Greek poet known for his didactic poems on hunting and fishing</note>:

> *But if you carry even a tiny piece cut from the skin of a hyena,*
> *Immediately puppies and fierce dogs,*
> *Stunned by bitter terror, shall not bark at you*
> *As you walk along, even if they had barked before.*

### *So that a dog cannot run.*

If you smear the wings <note>original: "alas," which usually means wings, but in an anatomical context for a dog could refer to the armpits or flanks</note> with oil, it will be hindered in its course; it happens in this way.

### *So that a hawk may be courageous.*

You shall encourage the bird against the prey, so that it attacks large birds; moisten the bait, which it uses during the hunting time, with wine; or if it is a goshawk <note>original: "astur"</note>, give it a little vinegar. When you want it to fly, give it three morsels of meat soaked in wine, or pour wine into a pigeon chick's beak, then make it fly. Thus,

### *You will make partridges more combative,*

If you give them sprigs of maidenhair fern <note>original: "adianti ramulos"</note> in their food, according to Pliny, and

### *Roosters become more combative,*

By giving them garlic in their food just before they are to fight; from which, most wittily in Old Comedy <note>Likely referring to the playwright Aristophanes</note>, they are called *garlic-fed* <note>original Greek: ἐσκοροδισμένοι (*eskorodisménoi*)</note>, that is, seasoned with garlic, a term for one who is vehement and too inclined toward battle.

### *Lest a bird fly high,*

Pluck the tail feathers that direct the course upward; thus it will fly below in a circle. If you wish

### *That a bird cannot fly,*

Cut the upper and lower nerves of the wing, and it remains without further harm <note>original: "sine noxa," implying the bird survives but is grounded</note>; the bird will not fly, and in this manner they do not escape from aviaries.

<summary>This page lists various traditional and magical methods for controlling animals during hunting, including ways to silence barking dogs, embolden hawks for falconry, and keep birds from escaping aviaries.</summary>
<keywords>fowling, falconry, hunting dogs, Pliny, Oppianus, folk magic, hawks, partridges, roosters, garlic-fed</keywords>

גבריאל מיכיאל ורופיאל אמן אמן אמן אמן סאלה הלליה כפי א א א א א א

### Translation

Ṭardi bath Oni (2) Hormisdar Ṭardi. In the name of AAAAAA, exorcised and sealed (3) are the Demon and the Devil and the Satan and the Curse-spirit and the evil Liliths (4) which appear by night and appear by day, and appear (to) Ṭardi bath [Oni, etc.]. (5) In the name of Gabriel, Michael, and Rophiel. Amen, Amen, Amen, Amen, Hallelia, Selah. According to AAAAAA.

### Commentary

A charm against ghosts. The interest of this bowl lies in the figure decorating the center. It represents a demon with arms and legs manacled. On either side of the figures is an enclosed space, that on the figure’s right hand bearing the inscription אסורא, that on its left, רשׁא, i. e. prohibition and permission. In the lower part of the body on the former side is inscribed the names of the sorcerer’s client. The pictures thus graphically presents the idea that the demon has no power over the lady in question. The picture is of better quality than the inscription, which is very illiterate. The spelling is most careless.

1. The connection of the proper names is uncertain, as also the character of the names themselves. For הרמסדר I might compare the Pahlavi *Ormazdyâr*, *Justi, p. 10a*.
2. For the repeated א, see p. 60.
3. לטאנא : probably an artificial form; cf. סטנא, טלנא, שׁידנא.

## UNIVERSITY MUSEUM. BABYLONIAN SECTION.

# No. 20 (Museum Number CBS 16023)

->In the name of Tardi, daughter of Oni<-

(2) Hormisdar Tardi. In the name of AAAAAA <note>The repeated letter Aleph often serves as a magical cipher or a call for divine attention</note>, exorcised and sealed (3) are the Demon and the Devil and the Satan and the Curse-spirit <note>original: *latana*</note> and the evil Liliths <note>dangerous night-demons of Mesopotamian folklore</note> (4) which appear by night and appear by day, and appear to Tardi, daughter of [Oni, etc.]. (5) In the name of Gabriel, Michael, and Rophiel <note>the archangels Gabriel, Michael, and Raphael</note>. Amen, Amen, Amen, Amen, Selah <note>a liturgical or musical pause</note>, Hallelujah. According to AAAAAA.

### Translation

Tardi, daughter of Oni (2) Hormisdar Tardi. In the name of AAAAAA, exorcised and sealed (3) are the Demon and the Devil and the Satan and the Curse-spirit and the evil Liliths (4) which appear by night and appear by day, and appear (to) Tardi, daughter of [Oni, etc.]. (5) In the name of Gabriel, Michael, and Rophiel. Amen, Amen, Amen, Amen, Hallelujah, Selah. According to AAAAAA.

### Commentary

A charm against ghosts. The interest of this bowl lies in the figure decorating the center. 

<note>The illustration depicts a demon with its arms and legs bound in manacles. On either side of the demon is an enclosed space; the space on the figure’s right side bears the inscription "Prohibition" </note><note>original: *asura*</note>, while the space on its left bears the inscription "Permission" <note>original: *resha*</note>. On the lower part of the demon's body, on the "Prohibition" side, the name of the client is written. This drawing graphically represents the idea that the demon is bound and has no legal or spiritual power over the woman.</note> 

The picture is of better quality than the inscription, which is very illiterate. The spelling is most careless.

1. The connection between the proper names is uncertain, as is the character of the names themselves. For **Hormisdar** <note>original: *hrmsdr*</note>, I might compare the Pahlavi <note>Middle Persian</note> name **Ormazdyar** <note>meaning "Friend of Ahura Mazda"</note>, found in Ferdinand Justi’s *Book of Iranian Names*, page 10a.
2. For the repeated letter **A** <note>original: א</note>, see the discussion on page 60.
3. **Latana** <note>original: *lt'n'*</note>: This is likely an artificial magical form created by adding a suffix; compare the similar forms for **Satan** <note>original: *stn'*</note>, **Talna** <note>original: *tln'*, a shadow-spirit</note>, and **Shidna** <note>original: *shydn'*, a demon-spirit</note>.

<summary>This page analyzes an Aramaic incantation bowl (No. 20) used to protect a woman named Tardi from various demons and spirits. It is distinguished by a central drawing of a manacled demon, symbolizing the spirit's lack of "permission" to harm the client.</summary>

<meta>This page is from the Sefer ha-Zohar, Parashat Emor (Folio 104). The layout is a single column of Zoharic text, including a section of the 'Ra'aya Meheimna' (The Faithful Shepherd). The script is Rashi script. The text discusses the spiritual significance of 'Ushpizin' (guests), charity to the poor, and the mystical meaning of the creation of man in the divine image.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

דחזות ליה חולקא בעמיא קדישא יתיר בכלא דמהימנותא לקבלא אושפיזין למחדי בהאי עלמא ובעלמא דאתי. ועבד בעי למחדי למסכני מט' בגין דחולקא דאינון אושפיזין דזמין למסכני הוא וההוא דיתיב בכלא דהמהימנותא ומין אושפיזין אלין עלאין אושפיזין מהימנותא ויהיב לון חולקיהון כלהו קיימי קמיה ואמרי:
> **אל תלחם את לחם רע עין וגו'** <note>משלי כג:ו</note>

השתכח דההוא פתורא דתקין דיליה הוא ולאו דקב"ה עליה כתיב:
> **וזרתי פרש על פניכם וגו' פרש חגיכם וגו'** <note>מלאכי ב:ג</note>

אוי ליה לההוא בר נש בשעתא דאינון אושפיזין מהימנותא קיימי מפתורא. ואמר רבי אבא אברהם כל ימוהי הוה קאים בפרשת אורחין לזמנא אושפיזין ולקבלא לון פתורא השתא דאזמנין ליה ולכלהו צדיקייא ולדוד מלכא ולא יהבין לון חולקהון ההוא קשיא מכולא ואקרי:
> **סורו נא מעל אהלי האנשים הרשעים האלה** <note>במדבר טז:כו</note>

וכלהו סלקין ואמרין: <term>יצחק</term> אמר:
> **ובטן רשעים תחסר** <note>משלי יג:כה</note>

<term>יעקב</term> אמר:
> **פתך אכלת תקיאנה** <note>משלי כג:ח</note>

ושאר כל צדיקייא אמרו:
> **כי כל שלחנות מלאו קיא צואה בלי מקום** <note>ישעיהו כח:ח</note>

<term>דוד מלכא</term> אמר והלכות דיכוי דכתיב ויהי כעפרת הימים וינוף יי' את ככל ומתי מחי קא מיירי בגין דדוד סחל לכבל והתעביד ליה אושפיזא ולא בעא ולא זמין ליה ולא יהב ליה חולקא וכחינון עטרה וימין דדוד מלכא דחין עלמא להלן עלוה ההוא בר נש דאטלים ליה כים יתיר מכלא. אמר ר' אלעזר בנ"כ חסידותא לא פטרת עליה דבר נש יתיר אלא במה דיכול דכתיב ליום כהנתת ידו וגו'. ולא לוחא אינוס חכחא והשבע וארוי קדמיתא ומה דישתאר לתן למסכני אף רוחא דכלא דאושפיזין הוא והיהו לאושפיזין ויהי לון קב"ה חלי עמיה ולברכה קרי עליה:
> **אז תתענג על יי' וגו'** <note>ישעיהו נח:יד</note>

ויצחק קארי עליה:
> **כל כלי יוצר עליך לא יצלח** <note>ישעיהו נד:יז</note>

אמר רבי שמעון האי דוד מלכא א"ל בגין דכל זינין דמלכא וקרבין למלכא בידוי דדוד אתפקדו. חכ"ז מאן דחדי גבור בחלקו ורעו וגו' קטן ועיסר כביט וגו' יעקב אמר לו ויבקע בבקר חורך וגו' שאר צדיקייא אמרו וכהך יי' תמיד והשביע וגו'. דוד מלכא אמר כל כלי יוצר עליך לא יצלח דהוא על כל זיני זינין אתפקד וכלה חולקיה דבר נש זכי לכל האי זכחן חולקיהון דצדיקייא בעלמא דין ובעלמא דאתי עליהו כתיב:
> **ועמך כלם צדיקים וגו'** <note>ישעיהו ס:כא</note>

---

### רעיא מהימנא (The Faithful Shepherd)

-> **ולקחתם לכם ביום הראשון וגו'** <- <note>ויקרא כג:מ</note>

**פקודא** דא ליטול לולב כדקא יאות ביומין אלין ויהי נמיכין וזיין ליה וקאי רזא דאוקימנא ולקחתם פדירוס כמה דקב"ה נטיל לון לישראל בהאי זימנא דדינון. אוף הכי ופרש בעיין ליה לקב"ה בחולקהון וחלוסן ביה. ולפ' קדמא דא לולב וזמין דכיה למיסב רזא דיוקנא דאדם וכן למטה. עב'.

הבקרח סמאי לככולי ברחמיו ובדתיו אף עשותיו. כל הבקרח סמיאי דא אדם דקב"ה קארי ליה סמאי דכתי' ויברא אלהים את האדם בצלמו ועוד דחקרי בבמיה בשעתא דחפיק קשוט וזיחא בעלמא וחקרי אלהים דכתיב אלהים לא תקלל קרא ליה בבמיה דכתיב ויברא אלהים

---

את האדם בצלמו ושפיר קא לוקימנא דכתיב **נעשה אדם בצלמנו כדמותנו** בשעתא דזווגא אתמר. וכך הוא כוונא דתרוייהו בנלס ודמות וחדס דדכר ונוקבא נפק ויברא אלהים את האדם בצלמו. כפכח דסליק מלכא אשכחנא דבשעתא דזווגא השתכח.

</vocab>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the festival of Sukkot from the previous folio, specifically focusing on the mystical guests (Ushpizin) and the ethical requirements of hospitality and charity during the festival. It transitions into the 'Ra’aya Meheimna' (The Faithful Shepherd) section regarding the commandment of the Four Species.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

One who sees his portion within the holy nation excels in all matters of faith by receiving the <term>Ushpizin</term> <note>The seven mystical "guests" or founding fathers who visit the Sukkah: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Aaron, Joseph, and David</note> to rejoice in this world and in the world to come. A person must bring joy to the poor, for the portion of those guests invited belongs to the poor. One who sits in the shadow of faith and invites these supernal guests—the guests of faith—but does not give them their portion <note>i.e., fails to feed the poor</note>, all of them stand over him and say:
> **"Do not eat the bread of a stingy man..."** <note>Proverbs 23:6; original: "Al tilcham et lechem ra ayin"</note>

It turns out that the table he prepared is his own, and not the Holy One's, blessed be He. Concerning him, it is written:
> **"I will spread dung upon your faces, the dung of your festival offerings..."** <note>Malachi 2:3; original: "Vezareti feresh al pneichem... feresh chageichem"</note>

Woe to that person at the time when those guests of faith rise from his table! Rabbi Abba said: All the days of Abraham, he would stand at the crossroads to invite guests and prepare a table for them. Now that [the poor] invite him, and all the righteous ones, and King David, and they are not given their portion, it is the most difficult thing of all, and it is called:
> **"Move away from the tents of these wicked men..."** <note>Numbers 16:26; original: "Suru na me'al ohalei ha'anashim ha-resha'im ha-eleh"</note>

And they all ascend and say: <term>Isaac</term> says:
> **"...but the belly of the wicked shall feel want."** <note>Proverbs 13:25; original: "U-beten resha'im techsar"</note>

<term>Jacob</term> says:
> **"The morsel you have eaten, you shall vomit up..."** <note>Proverbs 23:8; original: "Pitecha achalta teki'enah"</note>

And all the other righteous ones say:
> **"For all tables are full of vomit and filth, so that no place is clean."** <note>Isaiah 28:8; original: "Ki kol shulchanot mal'u ki tzo'ah bli makom"</note>

<term>King David</term> spoke of the laws of oppression... <note>The text here contains difficult Aramaic shorthand regarding David's role as the representative of the poor</note> because David was the "shield" for the poor, and he was made a guest, but [the host] did not want him, did not invite him, and did not give him his portion. Since King David is the "Crown" and the "Right Hand" that sustains the world, the person who deprives him is more condemned than anyone. Rabbi Eleazar said: A person is not exempted from acts of loving-kindness except by what he is able to do, as it is written: "according to the gift of his hand." One should not feel coerced, but should first satisfy himself and then give what remains to the poor; yet the spirit of all the guests remains with him. When the Holy One, blessed be He, rejoices with him, He calls out a blessing upon him:
> **"Then you shall delight in the Lord..."** <note>Isaiah 58:14; original: "Az ttit'anag al Hashem"</note>

And Isaac calls out over him:
> **"No weapon formed against you shall prosper..."** <note>Isaiah 54:17; original: "Kol kli yotzer alayich lo yitzlach"</note>

Rabbi Shimon said: King David says this because all the weapons of the King and the King's battles are entrusted to David's hand. Therefore, whoever rejoices with his portion... Jacob says to him: "Then your light shall break forth like the morning..." and the other righteous ones say: "And the Lord shall guide you continually and satisfy your soul..." King David says: "No weapon formed against you shall prosper," for he is appointed over all types of weapons. When a person merits all these merits, the portion of the righteous in this world and the world to come is written of them:
> **"Your people shall all be righteous..."** <note>Isaiah 60:21; original: "Ve-amech kulam tzaddikim"</note>

---

### The Faithful Shepherd (Ra'aya Meheimna)

-> **"And you shall take for yourselves on the first day..."** <- <note>Leviticus 23:40</note>

This **commandment** is to take the <term>Lulav</term> <note>The palm branch used on Sukkot</note> as is proper during these days... this is the secret of what we established: "And you shall take" refers to a redemption, just as the Holy One, blessed be He, took Israel at this time of judgment. So too, they should seek the Holy One, blessed be He, as their portion. The first [species] is the Lulav, which is prepared to take on the secret of the "Image of Man" (<term>Tzelem Adam</term>) and so it is below.

...The Holy One, blessed be He, called him "Image," as it is written: "And God created man in His own image." Furthermore, he is called by the name "Elohim" (God/Judge) at the time he brings truth and merit into the world... as it is written:

---

"Man in His image." And we have well established that it is written: **"Let us make man in our image, after our likeness"**—this was said at the time of the [divine] union. And such is the intention of both: "Image" (<term>Tzelem</term>) and "Likeness" (<term>Demut</term>) are one, emerging from the Male and Female. "And God created man in His image"—we find that at the time of the union, the King is present.

<summary>This page discusses the spiritual consequences of failing to share the festival meal with the poor, which insults the mystical guests (Ushpizin). It then transitions into a mystical explanation of the Lulav and the creation of man in the divine image.</summary>
<keywords>Ushpizin, Charity, Sukkot, King David, Lulav, Tzelem (Divine Image), Hospitality, Ra'aya Meheimna</keywords>

But when this is so, I do not see that one can doubt that in diminishing the velocity of the ascending stone, consuming it all, it can arrive at the state of rest before passing through all the degrees of slowness.

Simp. But if the degrees of greater and greater slowness are infinite, they will never be consumed; whence such an ascending heavy body will never bring itself to rest, but will move infinitely, always slowing down. A thing which is not seen to happen.

Salu. That would happen, Signor Simplicio, if the mobile went about lingering in each degree for some time; but it passes through them only without staying there beyond an instant. And because in any time, however small, there are infinite instants, they are therefore sufficient to correspond to the infinite degrees of diminished velocity. That such an ascending heavy body does not persist for any length of time in any same degree of velocity is made manifest thus: because if some length of time is assigned, at the first instant of such time, and also at the last, the mobile were to be found to have the same degree of velocity, it could from this second degree be equally pushed upward for an equal space, just as from the first it was carried to the second, and for the same reason it would pass from the second to the third, and finally would continue its uniform motion to infinity.

ནས། མཉམ་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱང་མཉམ་པ་ཉིད་ལ་མི་དམིགས་ན་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ཅི་ལས་#དགོངས་ཤེ་ན། མཐར་ཐུག་པའི་ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོའི་ས་ལ་ནི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ཆོས་ཐམས་ཅད་རྣམ་པར་སྨིན་པའི་བདག་ཉིད་དུ་གྱུར་ནས། སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་ངོ་བོ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་རྗེས་སུ་ཞུགས་ཏེ། 
དེ་བས་ན་དེ་ལ་དུས་གསུམ་#མཉམ་པ་ཉིད་ཅེས་བྱ་བ་ཡང་མེད་ལ། དུས་གསུམ་དུ་གཏོགས་པའི་སྦྱིན་པའི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ཡང་མེད་དོ། །དེའི་ཕྱིར། མཉམ་པ་ཉིད་ལ་འདས་པ་དང་། མ་འོངས་པ་དང་། ད་ལྟར་བྱུང་བའི་སྦྱིན་པའི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་དམིགས་པར་
ག་ལ་འགྱུར་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་གསུངས་སོ། །དེ་བཞིན་དུ་ཐམས་ཅད་ལ་ཡང་སྦྱར་བར་བྱའོ། །འགྲེས་ནི་དུས་གསུམ་མཉམ་པ་ཉིད་བསྩལ་#བའི་འགྲེས་དང་། ཆོས་ཐམས་ཅད་གཉིས་ཀྱི་སྒོ་ནས་བསྩལ་བའི་འགྲེས་དང་། ཕུང་པོ་ལྔའི་ཆོས་རྣམས་ལ་དུས་གསུམ་བསྩལ་བའི་འགྲེས་
དང་། སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ལ་དུས་གསུམ་དུ་གཏོགས་པའི་ཕུང་པོ་ལྔའི་ཆོས་རྣམས་བསྩལ་བའི་འགྲེས་དང་། དུས་གསུམ་མཉམ་པ་ཉིད་ལ་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་དྲུག་བསྩལ་བའི་འགྲེས་དང་། དེ་དག་ལ་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་བསྩལ་བའི་འགྲེས་དང་། དེ་དག་ཉིད་ལ་དྲན་པ་ཉེ་བར་གཞག་པ་
ལ་སོགས་པ་མ་འདྲེས་པའི་མཐར་ཐུག་པའི་བར་དག་བསྩལ་བའི་འགྲེས་དང་། སོ་སོ་#སྐྱེ་བོ་བསྩལ་བའི་འགྲེས་དང་། ཉན་ཐོས་དང་། རང་སངས་རྒྱས་དང་། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དང་། དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་བསྩལ་བའི་འགྲེས་རྣམས་སུ་ཤེས་པར་བྱའོ། །
དེ་བས་ན་འདི་ནི་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཆེན་པོ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོ་ཞེས་བྱའོ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནི་ཆེན་པོ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་ཐེག་པ་ཡིན་པས་ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོ་ཞེས་བྱ་བར་ངེས་པའི་ཚིག་གིས་བསྟན་ཏོ། །བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་གནས་བརྟན་རབ་འབྱོར་འདི་ནི་ཤེས་རབ་
english:
Since that itself is <term>kun brtags pa</term> <gloss>the imagined nature</gloss>, it does not exist. If emptiness does not exist, the meaning of the phrase "form would exist within it" is expressed as "it would transform into form."

After showing that the qualities such as the <term>paramita</term> <gloss>perfection</gloss> of generosity are not perceived within the equality of the three times <note>past, present, and future</note>, one might ask: what is intended by the statement, "If even equality itself is not perceived in equality?" On the level of the ultimate <term>Mahayana</term> <gloss>Great Vehicle</gloss>, all phenomena such as the perfections become the nature of full maturation. They follow the essence of emptiness. Therefore, in that state, even what is called the equality of the three times does not exist. Nor do the perfections of generosity and the rest, which belong to the three times, exist there. Consequently, the text asks: "How could the perfections of generosity of the past, future, and present be perceived within equality?" The same logic should be applied to all other factors.

The categories of analysis should be understood as follows:
*   The category of analyzing the equality of the three times.
*   The category of analyzing all phenomena through the gate of duality.
*   The category of analyzing the three times regarding the phenomena of the five <term>skandhas</term> <gloss>aggregates</gloss>.
*   The category of analyzing the phenomena of the five aggregates belonging to the three times within emptiness.
*   The category of analyzing the six perfections within the equality of the three times.
*   The category of analyzing emptiness within those perfections.
*   The category of analyzing everything from the <term>smrtyupasthana</term> <gloss>four applications of mindfulness</gloss> up to the final unmixed qualities.
*   The category of analyzing the <term>prthagjana</term> <gloss>ordinary beings</gloss>.
*   The categories of analyzing the <term>Sravakas</term> <gloss>Hearers</gloss>, <term>Pratyekabuddhas</term> <gloss>Solitary Realizers</gloss>, <term>Bodhisattvas</term>, and <term>Tathagatas</term> <gloss>Buddhas</gloss>.

Therefore, the phrase "This is called the Great Vehicle of the Bodhisattvas, the great beings" uses a definitive term to show that because it is the vehicle of great beings, it is called the Great Vehicle.

The Blessed One addressed the Elder Subhuti: "This is the wisdom..."

<summary>This page discusses the non-duality of the three times and the perfections within the state of emptiness. It explains the etymology of the Great Vehicle as being the path specifically for great beings who realize the equality of all phenomena.</summary>
<keywords>Great Vehicle, emptiness, three times, perfections, equality, Bodhisattva, Subhuti, aggregates</keywords>

ཡན་ལག་དང་། ཉིང་ལག་རྣམས་ལ་སྐྱེས་བུ་ཆེན་པོར་མངོན་པར་བྱེད་པ་#གང་ལ་ཡང་བྱེ་བྲག་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར། འདི་སྙེད་ཅིག་གོ་ཞེས་བྱ་བར་མི་རུང་བས་སུམ་ཅུ་རྩ་གཉིས་ཞེས་བྱ་བའི་གྲངས་དོན་མེད་#པར་འགྱུར་རོ་ཞེ་ན། དེ་ཡང་བདེན་མོད་ཀྱི་འོན་
ཀྱང་ཐོས་པ་དང་། དྲན་པ་དག་ལས་དེའི་རྗེས་སུ་འབྲང་བའི་དོན་#དེ་ལྟ་བུའི་གྲངས་ངེས་པར་#བསྟན་ཏེ། འདིར་ཡང་གྲངས་འདི་ཉིད་ཀྱིས་བསྟན་ཏོ། །མཚན་འདི་རྣམས་ཀྱང་མདོར་བསྟན་པ་དང་། བཤད་པ་དང་། རྒྱུ་དང་། འབྲས་བུ་དང་། རྣམ་པ་བཞིས་བསྟན་
ཏེ། དང་པོ་ནི་མདོར་བསྟན་པའོ། །དེའི་འོག་ཏུ་མཚན་དེ་རྣམས་འགྲེལ་པ་ནི་བཤད་པའོ། །སྔོན་གྱི་ལས་སྨོས་པ་#ནི་རྒྱུའོ། །སྔ་ལྟས་སྨོས་པ་ནི་འབྲས་བུའོ། །ཕྱག་དང་ཞབས་འཁོར་ལོའི་མཚན་དང་ལྡན་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ལ་འཁོར་ལོ་ནི་འཇིག་རྟེན་ན་རྣམ་པ་གཉིས་ཏེ། 
མཚོན་ཆའི་འཁོར་ལོ་དང་། འགྲོ་བ་འཇུག་པའི་འཁོར་ལོ་ཤིང་རྟ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་འཕང་#ལོ་ལྟ་བུའོ། །དེ་ཡང་ཕྱག་དང་ཞབས་གཉིས་ཀ་ལ་འབྱུང་ངོ་། །འདིའི་སྔོན་གྱི་ལས་ཀྱང་#རྣམ་པ་གཉིས་ཏེ། བླ་མ་ལ་#སྐྱེལ་ཞིང་བསུ་བའི་གྲངས་སུ་གཏོགས་པ་ཚུལ་
ཁྲིམས་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པས་བསྡུས་པ་ནི་གཅིག་སྟེ། དེའི་འབྲས་བུས་འགྲོ་བར་འཇུག་པའི་འཁོར་ལོ་ཞབས་ཀྱི་མཐིལ་དུ་འབྱུང་ངོ་། །ཆོས་ཉན་པ་དང་། ཕྲེང་བ་རྒྱུད་#པ་དང་། གཙུག་ལག་ཁང་དང་། མཆོད་རྟེན་གྱི་གན་དུ་འགྲོ་བ་དང་། གཡོག་བྱིན་པ་སྦྱིན་
པའི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པས་བསྡུས་པ་དེའི་འབྲས་བུས་ཕྱག་གི་མཐིལ་གཉིས་སུ་#འབྱུང་ངོ་། །འཁོར་ལོ་རྩིབས་སྟོང་དང་ལྡན་པ་མུ་ཁྱུད་ཅན་ལྟེ་བ་དང་བཅས་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་གང་གི་#ཚེ་འདི་གསུམ་ཡོངས་སུ་མ་རྫོགས་པ་དེའི་ཚེ་ནི་མཚན་དེ་དག་གིས་འཁོར་ལོས་སྒྱུར་#བར་གྱུར་
ནས་རབ་ཏུ་འབྱུང་བར་འགྱུར་རོ། །དེའི་ཚེ་ནི་མངོན་པར་རྫོགས་པར་འཚང་མི་རྒྱ་སྟེ། དཔེར་ན་རྒྱལ་པོ་ཤང་ཀ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ལྟ་བུའོ། །གང་གི་ཚེ་དེ་དག་ཐམས་ཅད་རྣམ་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་དུ་ཡོངས་སུ་རྫོགས་པར་གྱུར་པ་དེའི་ཚེ་མངོན་པར་རྫོགས་པར་འཚང་རྒྱ་
english: If one asks: Since the major limbs and minor appendages do not differ at all in their manifestation of a Great Being, and since it is inappropriate to say "it is exactly this many," does the number thirty-two not become meaningless? While that is true, nevertheless, based on what has been heard and remembered, the following definite number was taught in accordance with that meaning, and here also it is taught by this very number. These marks are presented in four ways: the brief summary, the detailed explanation, the causes, and the results. First is the brief summary. After that, the commentary on those marks is the detailed explanation. Mentioning the past actions <note>original: "karma"</note> is the cause. Mentioning the signs is the result. Regarding the phrase "having the marks of a wheel on the palms and soles," there are two types of wheels in the world: a wheel used as a weapon and a wheel used for movement, such as the wheel of a chariot. These appear on both the hands and the feet. The past actions for this are also of two types. One is included in the Perfection of Ethics <note>original: "shila-paramita"</note>, involving the practice of seeing off and welcoming Gurus; as a result of this, the wheel for movement appears on the soles of the feet. The other is included in the Perfection of Generosity <note>original: "dana-paramita"</note>, involving listening to the Dharma, stringing garlands, going to temples and stupas, and providing service; as a result of this, they appear on both palms. Regarding the phrase "having a wheel with a thousand spokes, a rim, and a hub," if these three features are not complete, one becomes a Universal Monarch <note>original: "chakravartin"</note> and then renounces the world. At that time, one does not attain perfect Buddhahood; an example is the king named Shanka and others. When all of these are complete in every aspect, one attains perfect Buddhahood.

->الفصل الرابع في قوانين مشتركة للقي والاسهال والاشارة الي كيفية<-
->جذب الدوا المسهل والقي<-

معها غيرها والمستفرغ يجب ان لا يبادر الي اغذية كثيرة وذمية فتجذبها الطبيعة غير مهضومة فان اوجب شي من ذلك فيجب ان يكون قليلا قليلا فتباعد حتي يكون بالتدرج ويكون الداخل في البدن مهضوما جيدا والفصد هو الاستفراغ الخاص بالسويه واما الاستفراغ الخاص بخلط بكثر وحده في كمية او بفسد في كيفية فهو غير الفصد وكل استفراغ افرط فانه يحدث جي في الاكثر ومن اورثه انقطاع اسهال كان معتادة علة لمعاودة ذلك الاستفراغ يربيها في الاكثر مثل من اورثه انقطاع وخذ اوخاط انفه سددا فان عودها يذهب به واعلم ان الباقية من المادة التي يحتاج الي استفراغها اقل قابلة من الاستقصاء والبلوغ به الي ان تخور القوة وكثيرا ما تحلل الطبيعة تلك البقية وما دام الخلط من الجنس الذي ينبغي والمريض يحمله فلا تخف من الافراط وربما احتجت ان تستفرغ الي الغشي ومن كانت قوته قوية ومادة اخلاطه الردية كثيرة فاستفرغه قليلا قليلا وكذلك اذا كانت المادة شديدة النضج او شديدة الاختلاط بالدم ولا يمكن ان يستفرغ دفعة واحدة كل يكون في عرق النسا وفي اوجاع المفاصل المزمنة وفي السرطان وفي الجرب المزمن والدماميل المزمنة واعلم ان الاسهال يجذب من فوق و يقلع من تحت فهو موافق للجذب المألوف والمواقف ايضا بعد استقرار المواد فاذا كانت المواد من تحت جذبها اليه خلاف وقلعها ايضا من حيث هي والتي بفعل الجذب وبالعكس والقصد يختلف حاله بحسب المواضع التي منها يؤخذ الدم علي ما علمت واقل الناس حاجة الي الاستفراغ من كان جيد الهضم واصحاب البلدان الحارة قليل الحاجة الي الاستفراغ

فنقول يستحب لمن اراد ان يستسهل ان يتقب او يفرق طعامه ثبتا واول قدر المبلغ الذي يتجربه في اليوم في موار وان يجعلها اطعمة مختلفة واشربه مختلفة ايضا فان المعدة تعرض لهامن هذه الحال ان يشتاق الي دفع ما فيها الي فوق اوالي تحت فاما الطعام الغير المختلف بل علي طعام اخرتان المعدة تشبع به وتضحي وتقبض عليه قبضا شديدا وخصوصا ان كان قليل المقدار واما اللين الطبيعة فلا ينبغي من ذلك شي واعلم ان الحاجة الي القي والاسهال ونحوهما غير واقعة بمن كان حسن التدبير يحتاج الي ما هو اخف منها وربما كفاه للهم فيه الرياضة والدلك والحجام ثم ان امتلأ بدنه تاكثر امتلاء مثله من اجود الاخلاط اعني من الدم فالقصد هو المحتاج اليه في تنقيته دون الاسهال فاذا اوجبت الضرورة فصدا او استفراغا بمثل الخريف وبالادن به القي به ابعد بالفصد هذا من وصايا ابقراط وكتب ابيلها وهو الحق وكذلك اذا كانت الاخلاط البلغمية مختلطة بالدم ولكي اذا كانت الاخلاط متساوية لزجة باردة فربما زادها الفصد غلظا ولزوجة فالواجب ان يبدأ بالاسهال وبالجملة ان كانت الاخلاط متساوية قدم الفصد فان غلب بعد ذلك استفراغ وان كانت غير متساوية استفراغ اولا الفضل حتي يتساوي ثم يفصد ومن قدم الدوا علي الفصد كان ينبغي ان يقدم الفصد ايا ما قليل ومن كان قرب العهد بالفصد واحتاج الي استفراغ فشرب الدوا اوقف له وكثيرا ما وقع شرب الدوا الواجب كان فيه الفصد في جي واضطراب فان لم يكن يسكن بالمسكنات فانه كان يجب ان يقدم عليه الفصد وليس لك استفراغ يحتاج اليه لفرط الامتلاء بقد تدعوا اليه عظم العلة والامتلاء بحسب الكيفية والكمية وكثيرا ما يعني تحسب التدبير عن الفصد الواجب في الوقت وكثيرا ما يدعوا الداعي الي الاستفراغ فيعارضه عارض فلانكون الحيلة فيه الاصوم والنوم وتدارك سو مزاج بوجه الامتلاء ومن الاستفراغ ما هو علي سبيل الاستظهار مثل ما يحتاج اليه من معتاده النقرس او الصرع اوغير ذلك في وقت معلوم وخصوصا في الربيع فيحتاج ان يستظهر قبل وقته ويستفرغ الاستفراغ الذي يختص به كان فصدا او اسهالا وربما كان استعمال المجففات من خارج والادوية الناسفة استفراغا مثل ما يفعل باصحاب الاستسقاء وقد يحوجك الي استعمال دوا مجانس للخلط المستفرغ في الكيفية كالسقمونيا عند حاجتك الي استفراغ الصفراء فيجب حينئذ ان يخلط به ما يخالفه في الكيفية و يوافقه في الاسهال كالهليلج وادارك سومزاج ان حدث عنه من بعد في اصحاب الاورام الاحشا فيضعف اسهالهم فان اضطررت الي ذلك فاستعمل لهم مثل اللبلاب والقرطم واما المسهل والخيار شنبر وكون ذلك قال ابقراط من كان قصبه سهل اجابة الطبيعة الي القي فالاول في تنقيته ان يستعمل القي في صيف اوربيع وقتها فان ذلك يومي البدن من التعب واعلم ان تعود الشارب ذربا لبن الطبيعة اوغير معتاد للقي الصيف ويتوقاه في غير موضع الحاجة ويجب ان يعقد قبل الاسهال والتي بطلبف الخلط الذي يريد استفراغه وتوسيع المجاري وقتها فان ذلك يومي البدن من التعب واعلم ان الشارب ذربا لبن الطبيعة اوغير معتاد للقي قبل استعمال الدوا القوي من احدي التدبير المقلة والاسهال والتي مع هزال المراق صعب وتعب وخلط والدوا الملقي قد يعود مسهلا اذا كانت المعدة قوية اوشرب علي شدة جوع اوكان الشارب ذربا لبن الطبيعة او لكون الدوا اوكان الدوا اثقل الجوهر من سريع النزول والمسهل يصبر مقيبا لضعف المعدة اوشدة الثقل او لكون الدوا كربها وكون صاحبه ذا تخم وكل دواء مسهل اذا لم يسهل غير نضج فانه يحرك الخلط الذي يسهله وينشره في البدن فيستولي علي البدن ويستجهل اليه اخلاط اخري فيكثر ذلك الخلط في البدن ومن الاخلاط ما هو اسرع اجابة الي القي في الاكثر كالاصفرا ومنها ماهو مستعصي علي القي كالسودا ومنها ماله حال كالحلبلب والنجوم اسهاله اصوب في نفسه ومن كان خلطه نازلا مثل اصحاب زلق الامعاء فتقبض الامعاء يعثر الدوا المسهلة ما هو مركب من ادية شديدة الاختلاف في زمان الاسهال فتضطرب الاسهال ويسهل الاول الثاني قبل ان يسهل الثاني وربما اسهل الاول نفس الثاني ومن تعرض للاسهال ويدنه نق به بد من دوا رو مغص وكرب يلحقه ويكون ما يستفرغ يستفرغ لصعوبة جدا وبالجملة الدوا ما يستفرغ الفضول فانه لا يكون معه اضطراب فاذا اخذ بضطراب فاما يستفرغ غير الفضل واذا تغير الخلط المستفرغ بقي او اسهال الي خلط اخر دل علي نقا البدن من الخلط المراد استفراغه

### The Fourth Art

->Chapter Four: On the Common Rules for Vomiting and Diarrhea, and an Indication of How to<-
->Attract [the Humor with] Purgative Medicines and Vomiting<-

...and other things with it. One who is being purged must not rush to consume large quantities of unwholesome food, lest nature draw it in undigested. If anything of this sort is required, it must be in very small amounts, spaced out gradually, so that what enters the body is well-digested. Phlebotomy <note>bloodletting</note> is a special kind of evacuation for equality <note>rebalancing the blood</note>. As for evacuation specific to an excess of a humor in quantity or corruption in quality, it is different from phlebotomy. Every evacuation that is excessive often causes harm. If the cessation of a habitual diarrhea leaves behind an ailment, the recurrence of that evacuation is often the remedy, such as when the cessation of a nosebleed causes obstructions; restoring the flow will remove them. 

Know that the remainder of the humor that needs to be evacuated is less capable of being thoroughly exhausted, and the strength of the body is depleted if one persists until it is gone. Nature often resolves that remainder on its own. As long as the humor is of the type that should be purged and the patient can bear it, do not fear excess. Sometimes you may need to purge until the patient faints. If someone has great strength and a large amount of corrupt humors, purge them little by little. This is also the case when the humor is extremely mature <note>well-digested or ready for elimination</note> or so mixed with blood that it cannot be purged all at once. This occurs in cases of sciatica, chronic joint pain, cancer, chronic scabies, and chronic boils. 

Know that diarrhea attracts from above and clears from below; thus, it agrees with the conventional method of attraction. It is also suitable after the materials have settled. If the materials are below, it draws them toward itself, clears them from where they are, and acts through attraction, and vice-versa. The state of phlebotomy differs according to the locations from which the blood is taken, as you have learned. Those who need evacuation the least are those with good digestion; inhabitants of hot climates have little need for evacuation.

We say it is recommended for one who wishes to be purged to break up or divide their food into several portions. The total amount to be taken during the day should be divided, and the foods and drinks should be varied. The stomach is prone in this state to desire to expel what is inside it, either upward or downward. As for food that is not varied—rather, relying on a single type—the stomach becomes satiated, becomes stagnant, and grips it tightly, especially if the amount is small. As for those with naturally loose bowels, none of this is needed. 

Know that the need for vomiting, diarrhea, and the like is not present in one who has a good regimen; they require things lighter than these. Perhaps exercise, massage, and cupping are sufficient for them. Then, if the body becomes filled with the best of humors, namely blood, then phlebotomy is what is needed for purification, not diarrhea. If necessity demands phlebotomy or evacuation, such as in autumn, and if it is not possible to use vomiting, it is better to use phlebotomy. This is one of the recommendations of Hippocrates and the books of the ancients, and it is the truth. Likewise, if phlegmatic humors are mixed with blood, and if the humors are uniform, viscous, and cold, phlebotomy might make them thicker and more viscous; thus, it is necessary to start with diarrhea. In summary, if the humors are uniform, prioritize phlebotomy; if they are not, evacuate the excess first until they become uniform, then perform phlebotomy. One who prioritizes medicine <note>purgative drugs</note> over phlebotomy should have performed phlebotomy for a short time first. If someone was recently bled and needs evacuation, and drinks the medicine, it will stop it. Often, taking the required medicine when phlebotomy was indicated leads to harm and agitation. If it does not subside with sedatives, phlebotomy should have been performed first. There is no evacuation required by excessive repletion as much as the severity of the ailment and the repletion—both in quality and quantity—demand. Often, good regimen takes the place of necessary phlebotomy at the time. Often, the need for evacuation arises, but an obstacle hinders it; the remedy then is fasting, sleep, and correcting the dyscrasia <note>imbalance of humors</note> in the manner of the repletion. 

There is evacuation done by way of prophylaxis, such as that required by those accustomed to gout, epilepsy, or other things at a known time, especially in spring. One needs to be proactive before the time arrives and perform the specific evacuation, whether phlebotomy or diarrhea. Sometimes the use of external desiccants and drying medicines is a form of evacuation, such as what is done for those with dropsy <note>edema</note>. Sometimes you are forced to use a medicine that is homogeneous in quality to the humor being evacuated, such as <term>saqmunya</term> <gloss>scammony</gloss> when you need to evacuate bile. In that case, you must mix it with something that opposes it in quality but agrees with it in purging, such as <term>halilaj</term> <gloss>myrobalan</gloss>. To correct a dyscrasia that occurs later in those with tumors in the viscera, their diarrhea may weaken them; if you are forced to do so, use things like ivy and safflower for them. As for the purgative and <term>khiyar shanbar</term> <gloss>cassia fistula</gloss>, Hippocrates said: "Whoever has a stomach that is easily moved to vomit, the first step in their purification is to use vomiting in summer or spring when the time is right." This rids the body of fatigue. Know that if the person drinking it is accustomed to a loose stool or is not accustomed to vomiting, they should avoid it in times when it is not needed. It is necessary to prepare before diarrhea by thinning the humor one wishes to evacuate and widening the passages at that time, as this rids the body of fatigue. Know that the one who drinks it—if they are accustomed to a loose stool or are not accustomed to vomiting—should [use] one of the reducing regimens before using a strong medicine. Diarrhea with abdominal flaccidity is difficult and tiring. A purgative medicine may act as a laxative if the stomach is strong, if taken during extreme hunger, or if the person is accustomed to a loose stool, or if the medicine is heavier in essence than in speed of descent. The purgative may remain, causing trouble due to the weakness of the stomach, extreme heaviness, or because the medicine irritates it, or the person has indigestion. Every purgative medicine, if it does not purge the undigested humor, stirs up the humor it is meant to purge and spreads it throughout the body, dominating the body and attracting other humors to it, increasing that humor in the body. Among the humors, some are quicker to respond to vomiting, such as bile. Some are resistant to vomiting, such as black bile. Some have a condition like milk and stars <note>obscure metaphorical or astrological reference</note>; its diarrhea is safer in itself. Whoever has a humor flowing downward, such as those with intestinal slippage, the gripping of the intestines hinders the purgative medicine. That which is composed of medicines that are strongly different during the time of diarrhea causes the diarrhea to become agitated; the first will purge the second before the second can purge, and perhaps the first will purge the very same second. Whoever is exposed to diarrhea and their body is not cleansed of it, it must be from a drug or colic and distress that befalls them, and what is evacuated is evacuated with great difficulty. In general, if a medicine evacuates the waste, there will be no agitation with it. If it is taken with agitation, then either it is evacuating what is not waste, or if the evacuated humor changes through vomiting or diarrhea to another humor, it indicates the purification of the body from the humor intended to be evacuated.

english: Thus, meditation is not pointless; for if the perfection of meditation is lacking, it is impossible to make it manifest. As it has been said: "The path that extracts the thorn of existence was shown to you by me. The Tathagata is the shower; you must strive for yourselves." If so, for the path that transcends the world, it would follow that co-emergent joy is directly perceived by those who engage in desire. If even the oral instructions are pointless for that, what need to mention meditation? If one asks what is the use of another's oral instructions for a matter of direct perception, it is said: "Merit," and so forth. This is the intent: here, the worldly co-emergent joy itself is not the thing to be accomplished, because it is already established, and because it is inferior to the bliss of the higher and higher god realms, etc. Because it is accompanied by taints <note>Sanskrit: āsrava</note>, it is impurity itself, and thus it is the very root of the faults of those in cyclic existence. Then what is it like? That which is the individual perfect awareness of the Tathagatas, the co-emergent Dharma Body <note>Sanskrit: dharmakāya</note> which is like space, and the co-emergent Enjoyment Body <note>Sanskrit: sambhogakāya</note> which arises in accordance with its cause—the most excellent, perfectly pure co-emergent characterized by certain bliss—that is what is to be accomplished here. Furthermore, since it is not realized by other means, the perfection of meditation through superior devotion to the oral instructions on the worldly co-emergent joy itself leads to manifestation, which is known by oneself. It is not so from the very beginning; therefore, hearing, contemplation, and meditation are not pointless here. "Method" is the path. "Relying on that" is authentic meditation. "Succession of many" means many types. "Obtained from the Guru" refers to the Guru's timing; the Guru should bestow it according to the ritual to a student who is a suitable vessel for the lineage; this is the meaning of "bestowing the pith instructions."

<header>POLITICS</header>

<margin>for different purposes <note>original: ἄλλον ἄλλην .H.</note></margin> the pilot, and the shipowner the pilot; for one understands the stern, the other the prow, and they apply their skills to the rigging or the drum. Just as the architect has assistants and craftsmen who do not ruin his work but work together to complete it properly, the statesman is a master craftsman of sorts and a creator of power and justice. He will not immediately choose friends who are identical to himself, or servants and co-purchasers for the sake of goodness, but rather [he chooses] one for one need and another for another, because [of the pressure of those who] act against him unjustly and violently. For he said that it makes no difference to a builder or carpenter whether a person is inexperienced and uses rulers and levels incorrectly, as this would cause the work to become distorted. Friends are indeed the living and thinking instruments of political men; and one should not join them when they overstep, but rather pay attention so that they do not commit errors even through ignorance.
<margin>friends <note>original: φίλοι .H.</note></margin> This is what concerned Solon regarding his friends. For when he knew that he had taken the debts to lighten them by the <term>seisachtheia</term> <gloss>shaking off of burdens</gloss>, and the promise was to introduce a cancellation of debts, he shared this with his friends. The latter, however, acted wickedly and took advantage; for they preemptively borrowed much silver, and after a short time, when the law was brought to light, they were seen to have purchased bright houses and much land with the money they had borrowed. Solon bore the blame for being a co-conspirator. Through ignorance of his friends' ambitions, he himself became the weakest and most humble of them, like the Pegasus of Euripides, retreating and yielding more than he wished. By assisting in their misfortunes more than he should have, he seemed to be complicit in their injustices. For to save a man who is being punished—like pushing a fire that is rolling along—is to invite the commands that come with it. By nature, such men err greatly, and he bore the shame of his actions, as if eating the bitter fruit of hunger. He cast himself into dishonor while protecting his allies, and he managed to get them released out of an erotic devotion. Being softened by one, he feared writing a letter to a certain ruler on his behalf. Nicias, if he does not act unjustly, he is not unjust, and if he acts unjustly, he is still not [necessarily] unjust; but Phocion did not even join his son-in-law, who was involved in a lawsuit regarding stolen goods, but saying "I made you my son-in-law for all that is just," he walked away. And Timoleon the Corinthian, when he could not persuade his brother to stop his tyranny through teaching and entreaty, joined those who executed him. For it is not the goal to be a friend "up to the altar" <note>a Greek proverb meaning to support a friend only insofar as it does not violate religious duty</note>, as Pericles once said, but up to the limit of law, justice, and the common good. He who is overlooked brings great damage to the public, as [Antiphon] said regarding not giving justice to Strophios or Phoebidas; for these were the very people who plunged the Lacedaemonian city into war. Since it is a heavy thing to trample on the moderate errors of friends, the political argument does not force one to do so, but rather, by placing the greatest public matters in a secure position, one should assist friends from one’s own resources, and stand by them, and work with them. There are also these graces [to offer]: to assist a friend in obtaining an office; or rather, to entrust him with an administration, a reputation, or a humane embassy—such as one having the honors of a leader, or a mission to a city for the sake of friendship and harmony. For this trust is correct, and their action is clear and great, provided it is done first for oneself, and then by sending the friend, like Diomedes: "If you command me to choose a companion, how could I forget noble Odysseus?" And he in turn likewise gave him equal praise for his own deeds. "There are other noble arrivals whom you might urge, of the Thracians, whom noble Diomedes met, and killed twelve of their leaders, all best." For

this yielding toward friends does not at all adorn the one who praises those who praise him. But obstinacy, says Plato, is the neighbor of solitude. Furthermore, alongside these graces of humanity, one should also contribute non-friendship; for one should not command that those who are not present be praised or loved, as one has been the cause and contributor to their status. One should put aside base or absurd requests, not bitterly, but teaching and comforting them gently, that such things are not worthy of their virtue or reputation. Epaminondas did this best: arriving to Menexenus, to whom Pelopidas had left a guard to free him from the virtue of his deeds, and not long after having left those things, he said he was taking the needs of Pelopidas as if for treasuries or generals. But someone who is heavy and obstinate—since Catulus the censor, who was a friend, sought from him a treasury that was being managed by him—said, "It is shameful, you, who should be correcting us young men, to be expelled by our own servants." For by refusing the need quickly with anger, one removes the heaviness and bitterness from the word, as one who does not offer the pain willingly, but necessarily, because of the law and justice. There are also ways in politics that are not ignoble regarding the finances of friends in need, such as Themistocles, who after the battle saw a dead man wearing golden bracelets and a necklace; he himself passed by, but turning to a friend, he said, "Pick these up, for you have not become Themistocles." For affairs often grant this to the statesman regarding friends; for they are not all warriors, and if one is not in need, one can help in other ways regarding justice, and for those who are bound to him, he provides care and protection, and to another, cooperation in a contract, or a contribution of aid. Epaminondas, when a friend approached him, commanded him to ask for a talent, as if his slave had commanded it. When the person who was asked came and inquired, he said first, "Because this man is good, he is poor; but you are wealthy, having embezzled much from the city." And Xenophon says that most men admire their friends who are superior to money. Since one must become a "bulwark" to all, and every political life bears some enmities and differences, it is not least appropriate that the politician knows this. Many praise the way Themistocles and Aristides would put aside their enmity whenever they were sent on an embassy or military command, and then take it up again. And how Cretinus was extraordinarily pleasing to the Magnesian! Who, while engaging in politics with his opponent—not with a blow, but with a soul that was ambitious and brilliant—when the war saw the city in danger due to the beard of Mithridates, he ordered the one who had taken the power to manage affairs while he himself stepped aside. "If he wishes to be the general, I shall depart so that we do not destroy the city by being ambitious against each other." The challenge pleased the army, and having decided that it was more warlike for him to be a woman, he withdrew with his children and wife. For Cretinus sent him off, having given him his own money, which was more useful to those fleeing or besieged, and he saved the city from being destroyed by a command that had come from nowhere, unexpectedly. For if noble and wise men do not disappear, "I love my friends, but I love my fatherland even more." For not wishing to be dissolved into enmity, for the sake of which one must sacrifice a friend, is terribly savage and beastlike.

<summary>This section focuses on the proper political conduct of statesmen regarding the selection of friends, the management of debts and public funds, and the necessity of prioritizing the state over personal ambition or personal loyalties.</summary>

म० टी०—अस्मादेव सम्यग्व्यवसायात्स हित्वा दुराचारताम्—

> क्षिप्रं भवति धर्मात्मा शश्वच्छान्तिं निगच्छति ॥

चिरकालमधर्मात्माऽपि मद्भजनमहिम्ना क्षिप्रं शीघ्रमेव भवति धर्मात्मा धर्मानुगतचित्तो दुराचारत्वं झटित्येव त्यक्त्वा सदाचारो भवतीत्यर्थः। किं च शश्वन्नित्यं शान्तिं विषयभोगस्पृहानिवृत्तिं निगच्छति नितरां प्राप्नोत्यतिनिर्वेदात्। काश्चिन्मद्भक्तः प्रागभ्यस्तं दुराचारवमत्यजन्न भवेदपि धर्मात्मा, तथा च स नश्येदेवेति नेत्याह भक्तानुकम्पापरवशतया कुपित इव भगवान्—नैतदाश्चर्यं मन्वीथा हे कौन्तेय निश्चितमेवेदशं मद्भक्तेर्माहात्म्यम्। अतो विप्रतिपन्नानां पुरस्तादपि त्वं प्रतिजानीहि सावज्ञं सगर्वं च प्रतिज्ञां कुरु न मे वासुदेवस्य भक्तोऽतिदुराचारोऽपि प्राणसंकटमापन्नोऽपि सुदुर्लभयोग्यः सन्प्रार्थ्यमानोऽपि अतिमूढोऽशरणोऽपि न प्रणश्यति किं तु कृतार्थ एव

<header>Srimad Bhagavad Gita.</header> [Chapter 9, Verses 30-31]

**Shridhara Swami’s Commentary:** If you give liberation only to devotees and not to non-devotees, then do you not have a disparity caused by likes and dislikes? He replies: "Equal..." I am equal toward all beings; therefore, there is no one who is dear or hateful to Me. Despite this being so, those who worship Me, they are devotees, and they dwell in Me. And I, too, am in them as their benefactor. The meaning is this: just as fire, while removing the cold and darkness of those who serve it, does not exhibit disparity, or as the wish-fulfilling tree does, similarly, I, despite favoring My devotees, have no disparity; rather, this is the glorious power of devotion to Me. <note>29</note>

**Madhusudana Saraswati’s Commentary:** Furthermore, the glorious power of devotion to Me is such that it creates a disparity even where there is equality; hear of that glory:

> Even if a person of very wicked conduct 
> Worships Me with exclusive devotion, 
> He should be considered righteous, 
> For he has resolved correctly. <note>30</note>

Whoever, even one of very wicked conduct, like Ajamila and others, worships Me with exclusive devotion—through the awakening of some good fortune—should be considered righteous, even if he was previously wicked. Because "he has resolved correctly"—he has the resolve of a righteous person. <note>30</note>

**Shridhara Swami’s Commentary:** Furthermore, showing that the effect of devotion to Me is inconceivable, he says: "Even if..." Even a man of extremely wicked conduct, if he worships Me, Sri Narayana, without performing devotion to other deities, he should be considered righteous, indeed superior. Because he has resolved correctly, having made the noble resolve: "I shall be fulfilled by worshipping the Supreme Lord." <note>30</note>

**Madhusudana Saraswati’s Commentary:** From this correct resolve, he abandons his wicked conduct:

> Quickly he becomes righteous, 
> And attains eternal peace. 
> O Kaunteya, know this for certain: 
> My devotee is never lost. <note>31</note>

Even though he was wicked for a long time, by the glory of worshiping Me, he "quickly becomes righteous"—his mind becomes focused on dharma, abandoning wicked conduct immediately and becoming one of good conduct. Furthermore, he "attains eternal peace"—he attains a constant state of peace, meaning the withdrawal of thirst for sensory enjoyment, due to extreme detachment. If one were to think that My devotee might not become righteous, having not abandoned previously practiced wicked conduct, and thus would be destroyed, he says "No"—as if angry, being overcome by compassion for His devotee: Do not think of this as surprising, O Kaunteya; the greatness of devotion to Me is certainly just this. Therefore, even before those who are skeptical, declare it with conviction and pride: "My devotee—the devotee of Vasudeva—even if he is of very wicked conduct, even if he is in a life-threatening situation, even if he has failed in all attempts at practice, even if he is being prayed for [by others], even if he is foolish and has no other refuge, he is never lost; rather, he becomes fulfilled." The examples of Ajamila, Prahlada, Dhruva, Gajendra, and others are well-known. And the scripture says: "No evil ever befalls the devotees of Vasudeva." <note>31</note>

<summary>This page explains that through the power of exclusive devotion, even the most wicked individuals are swiftly transformed into righteous beings, as the Lord promises that His devotee will never perish.</summary>
<keywords>Devotion, Wickedness, Righteousness, Transformation, Promise, Vasudeva, Peace</keywords>

2. The <term>mark of continuity</term>: Relying on wisdom, it generates consciousness of suffering and joy; thoughts arise and associate without interruption.

In the second, the <term>mark of continuity</term>, "relying on wisdom" explains the basis of its arising; it means relying on the previous discrimination of loving objects to generate the sensation of joy, and regarding non-loving objects to generate the sensation of suffering. Repeatedly generating thoughts, it continuously manifests. This explains the self-continuity. It can also generate defilements to nourish karma, inducing and sustaining birth-and-death, thereby causing the continuity of others. The lower text says "sustaining suffering and joy." Therefore, it says "generates [consciousness]... without interruption."

3. The <term>mark of grasping</term>: This means that regarding the previous objects of suffering and joy, one does not understand they are empty and unreal, and thus deeply initiates grasping.

<summary>The text defines the marks of continuity and grasping, explaining how the failure to see reality leads to sustained suffering and attachments.</summary>

4 Alterum Veteris & Noui testamenti discrimen statuitur in figuris, quòd illud absente veritate, imaginem tantùm & pro corpore vmbram ostentabat: hoc præsentem veritatem & corpus solidū exhibet. Atque huius fere fit mentio vbicunque veteri testamento nouum opponitur: fusior tamen est eius tractatio in epistola ad Hebræos quàm alibi vsquam. Illic disputat Apostolus aduersus eos qui Legis Mosaicæ obseruationes aboleri posse non puta-bant nisi vt secum traherent religionis totius ruinam. Quo hunc errorem refutet, assumit <margin>Psal. 110. b. 4</margin> quod de Christi sacerdotio prædictum apud Prophetam fuerat. nam quum æternum illi deferatur sacerdotium, certū est aboleri sacerdotium illud vbi alii aliis successores quoti-die substituebantur. Præualere autem noui istius sacerdotis institutionem probat, quòd <margin>Heb. 7. b. 11. c. 19. & 9. c. 9. & 10. a. 1</margin> iuramento stabilitur. Subiungit postea, in ea sacerdotii translatione verti etiam Testamē-ti mutationem. Atque id necessarium fuisse ratione cōfirmat, quoniam ea erat Legis im-becillitas quæ nihil adducere ad perfectionē posset. Tum deinde prosequitur quæ illa fue-rit imbecillitas, nēpe quòd externas carnis iustitias habuerit quæ cultores suos non possēt secundū conscientiam perfectos reddere, quòd pecudum victimis, nec peccata delere, nec veram sanctitatem conciliare poterat. Concludit ergo, vmbram fuisse in ipsa futurorum bonorum, non viuam rerum effigiem: ideoque non aliud habuisse officii nisi vt introdu-ctio esset in spem meliorem quæ in Euangelio exhibetur. Hic videndum est qua parte fœ-dus Legale cum fœdere Euangelico, Christi ministerium cum Mosaico conferatur. Nam si ad promissionum substantiam pertineret comparatio, magnum extaret inter duo Testa-menta dissidium: sed quum status quæstionis aliò nos ducat, eò tendendum est vt verū re-periamus. Fœdus ergo quod æternum & nunquam interiturum semel sanciuit, in medio statuamus. Illius complementum, vnde tandem habet vt statum ratúmque sit, Christus est. Talis confirmatio dum expectatur, ceremonias Dominus per Mosen præscribit, quæ sunt velut solennia confirmationis symbola. Id in contentionem veniebat, cederéne oporteret Christo quæ in Lege ordinatæ erant ceremoniæ. Hæ verò tametsi fœderis duntaxat acci-dentia erant, vel certè accessiones ac annexa, & (vt vulgus loquitur) accessoria: quia tamen instrumenta erant illius administrandi, fœderis nomen habent. qualiter & aliis Sacramē-tis dari solet. Proinde, in summa, Vetus testamentum hoc loco appellatur solennis confir-mandi fœderis ratio, ceremoniis & sacrificiis cōprehensa. En ia quoniā nihil solidū subest, nisi vlterius transeatur, oportuisse antiquari & abrogari cōtendit Apostolus, vt Christo po-tioris Testamenti sponsori ac mediatori locus daretur, per quem æterna sanctificatio ele-ctis semel acquisita est: & transgressiones obliteratæ, quæ sub Lege manebant. Quòd si ma-lis, ita accipe: vetus fuisse Domini Testamentum, quod vmbratili & inefficaci ceremonia-rum obseruatione inuolutum tradebatur. ideoque temporarium fuisse, quia veluti in su-spenso erat, donec firma & substantiali confirmatione subniteretur. Tum verò demū no-uum æternúmque factum fuisse, postquam Christi sanguine consecratum stabilitúmque fuit. Vnde calicem, quem discipulis in Cœna porrigit Christus, Noui testamenti calicem <margin>Matt. 26. c. 28</margin> vocat in suo sanguine: vt significet, tum verè Dei Testamento suam constare veritatē, per quam nouum fit & æternum dum sanguine suo obsignatur.

5 Hinc liquet quo sensu dixerit Apostolus, Legis pædagogia deductos fuisse Iudæos ad <margin>Galat. 3. d. 24. & 4. a. 1</margin> Christum antequam ipse in carne exhiberetur. Illos quoque filios & hæredes Dei fuisse fa-tetur: sed qui propter pueritiam sub pædagogi custodia habendi essent. Cōueniebat enim, sole iustitiæ nondum exorto, nec tantum esse reuelationis fulgorem, nec tantā intelligen-di perspicaciam. Sic ergo verbi sui lucem illis Dominus dispensauit, vt eam eminus adhuc & obscurè cernerent. Ideo hanc intelligentiæ tenuitatem pueritiæ vocabulo Paulus notat, quā elementis huius mundi & externis obseruatiūculis, tanquā regulis puerilis disciplinæ, voluit Dominus exerceri, donec effulgeret Christus: per quē fidelis populi cognitionē ado-lescere oportebat. Hanc distinctionem signauit Christus ipse, quum diceret, Legem & Pro- <margin>Matth. 11. b. 13</margin> phetas fuisse vsque ad Iohannem: ex eo euangelizari regnum Dei. Quid Lex & Prophetæ sui temporis hominibus prodiderūt? nempe gustum præbebant eius sapientiæ quæ olim ad liquidum manifestanda erat, & procul emicantem præmonstrābant. Vbi autem digito potest ostendi Christus, referatum est regnum Dei. In ipso enim expositi sunt thesauri o- <margin>Coloss. 2. b. 9</margin> mnes sapientiæ & intelligentiæ, quibus propè ad ipsa cæli adyta penetratur.

english:
But we shall easily be disentangled from such scruples if we turn our mind to that dispensation of God which I have noted: that he wished, for the time when he was still delivering his Testament in some way wrapped up to the Israelite people, to signify and figure both the grace of future and eternal happiness by earthly benefits, and the gravity of spiritual death by bodily punishments.

4. Another distinction between the Old and New Testament is established in figures, in that the former, with the truth absent, showed only an image and a shadow instead of the body: the latter exhibits the present truth and the solid body. And this is mentioned almost everywhere the new is opposed to the old testament: yet its discussion is fuller in the epistle to the Hebrews than anywhere else. There, the Apostle disputes against those who did not think that the observances of the Mosaic Law could be abolished without dragging with them the ruin of the whole of religion. To refute this error, he assumes what had been predicted of Christ’s priesthood by the Prophet. For since an eternal priesthood is conferred upon him, it is certain that that priesthood is abolished where successors were substituted for others daily. He proves that the institution of this new priest prevails, because it is established by an oath. He subsequently adds that the change of the Testament is also involved in that translation of the priesthood. And he confirms that this was necessary by reason, since such was the weakness of the Law that it could bring nothing to perfection. Then he proceeds to what that weakness was, namely, that it had external justices of the flesh which could not render its worshippers perfect according to conscience, because by the victims of beasts, it could neither wipe away sins nor procure true holiness. He concludes, therefore, that it was a shadow in the very thing of future goods, not a living image of the things: and therefore it had no other office than to be an introduction into the better hope which is exhibited in the Gospel. Here it must be seen in what part the Legal covenant is compared with the Evangelical covenant, the ministry of Christ with the Mosaic. For if the comparison pertained to the substance of the promises, a great disagreement would exist between the two Testaments: but since the state of the question leads us elsewhere, we must tend toward finding the truth. Let us therefore place in the middle the covenant which he once ratified as eternal and never to perish. Its complement, from which it finally has that it stands firm and ratified, is Christ. While such confirmation is awaited, the Lord prescribes ceremonies through Moses, which are as it were the solemn symbols of confirmation. This came into contention: whether the ceremonies that were ordained in the Law ought to yield to Christ. These indeed, although they were only accidents of the covenant, or certainly accessions and annexes, and (as the common people say) accessories: because, however, they were instruments of administering it, they have the name of the covenant, just as is accustomed to be given to other Sacraments. Therefore, in sum, the Old Testament is called in this place the solemn manner of confirming the covenant, comprised in ceremonies and sacrifices. Now, since nothing solid lies underneath, unless one passes further, the Apostle contends that it ought to have been made obsolete and abrogated, so that place might be given to Christ, the sponsor and mediator of a better Testament, through whom eternal sanctification has been once acquired for the elect: and the transgressions, which remained under the Law, were obliterated. But if you prefer, take it this way: the Old Testament was that which was delivered wrapped in the shadowy and ineffective observation of ceremonies; and therefore it was temporary, because it was, as it were, in suspense, until it was supported by a firm and substantial confirmation. But then finally it became new and eternal, after it was consecrated and stabilized by the blood of Christ. Whence the cup, which Christ offers to the disciples at the Supper, he calls the cup of the New Testament in his blood: to signify that then the truth of God’s Testament truly consists, by which it is made new and eternal while it is sealed by his blood.

5. From this it is clear in what sense the Apostle said that the Jews were led to Christ by the pedagogy of the Law before he himself was exhibited in the flesh. He admits that they were also children and heirs of God: but who were to be held under the custody of a pedagogue because of their childhood. For it was fitting, with the sun of justice not yet risen, that there should be neither such splendor of revelation nor such perspicacity of understanding. Thus, therefore, the Lord dispensed the light of his word to them, so that they perceived it still from afar and obscurely. Therefore, Paul notes this thinness of intelligence with the word "childhood," by which the Lord wished them to be exercised with the elements of this world and external little observances, as rules of childish discipline, until Christ should shine forth: through whom the knowledge of the faithful people had to grow up. Christ himself marked this distinction when he said that the Law and the Prophets were until John: from then on the kingdom of God is evangelized. What did the Law and the Prophets profit the men of their time? Namely, they provided a taste of that wisdom which was one day to be manifested in clarity, and they pointed out that which was shining from afar. But when Christ can be pointed out with the finger, the kingdom of God has been opened. For in him are exposed all the treasures of wisdom and intelligence, by which one penetrates almost to the very inner sanctuaries of heaven.

while the things done in it through the divine plan flow down to us beneficially, as to those born of God. Therefore, in my opinion, according to the hierarchical sense handed down by God, the divine leaders of our sacred order call this most venerable and holy mystery of the <term>Ointment</term> <gloss>original Greek: Myron</gloss> a <term>telete</term> <gloss>consecration or perfecting rite</gloss>, because it actually consecrates and perfects. It is as if one spoke of the "consecration of God," praising his divine perfection in both senses. For it is the consecration of God, both because he is sanctified in a human way for our sake, and because he himself, in a divine way, consecrates and sanctifies everything that is to be consecrated. Furthermore, those who know Hebrew say that the sacred melody of the divinely inspired prophets signifies the praise of God, or "Praise the Lord" <note>original: "Laudate Dominum", referring to the word Alleluia</note>. Since, therefore, every sacred appearance of God and every divine operation is described in the varied composition of hierarchical symbols, it is by no means out of place to remember the praise of the prophets which they learned from God. For it teaches clearly and holily that the divine benefits are worthy of the highest praise.

...while the things done in them through the divine plan flow down to us beneficially, as to those born of God. From this, I believe, according to the hierarchical mind and divine tradition, the divine leaders of our hierarchy call this most venerable ceremony the <term>consecration of the Ointment</term> <gloss>original Greek: Myrou teleten</gloss>, naming it from the actual perfecting it performs. It is as if one said "the consecration of God," praising its divine perfecting power in both meanings. For it is his consecration, both in his being sanctified in a human manner for us, and in his divine performing and sanctifying of all things that are consecrated. Those who know the language of the Hebrews say that the sacred melody of the divinely inspired prophets signifies the praise of God, or "Praise the Lord." Since every sacred manifestation of God and divine operation is inscribed in the varied arrangement of hierarchical symbols, it is not unfitting to mention the divinely-moved song of the prophets. It teaches, in a way both pure and fitting for sacred things, that the divine acts of goodness are worthy of sacred praise.

This is the fifth unshared quality.

The statement "he has no equanimity that is not investigative" means that just as Arhats might neglect the welfare of sentient beings without investigation, the Tathagata does not do so. He sets things aside only after investigating the time and the non-time, the fortunate and the unfortunate, the meaningful and the meaningless, and not otherwise; this is the sixth.

"He has no loss of aspiration." "He has no loss of diligence." "He has no loss of mindfulness." "He has no loss of meditative concentration." "He has no loss of wisdom." "He has no loss of liberation." "He has no loss of the wisdom-vision of liberation." These mean that Arhats, due to the nature of their sphere of activity, do not naturally generate aspiration for the level of a Buddha or the activities of a Buddha, but rather aspire only to the deeds of a Listener <note>Sravaka</note>. Likewise, the diligence, mindfulness, meditative concentration, wisdom, liberation, and wisdom-vision of liberation belonging to the level of a Buddha are not present in the Listeners. Therefore, by not attaining those seven phenomena like aspiration and so forth, they are "lost" in the sense of being deficient.

The Buddhas are never without the attainment of these distinguished qualities. Since they have understood all phenomena, they do not have even the slightest loss. In this way, the Buddhas' aspiration to act for the benefit of sentient beings arises uninterruptedly at all times. Their aspiration toward phenomena like great love and great compassion, teaching the Dharma, maturing sentient beings, and—having perfectly adopted the Bodhicitta <note>mind of awakening</note>—their aspiration to never interrupt the lineage of the Three Jewels, arises uninterruptedly. ཡེ་ཤེས་བདེ་བ་ཆེན་པོའི་རང་བཞིན་ནི་འཁྲུལ་བའི་མཚན་མ་ཐམས་ཅད་ནུབ་པས་སྤྲོས་པ་མེད་པའོ། །ཡང་དག་པའི་ཡེ་ཤེས་འདི་ཉིད་ཀྱི་ས་བོན་དང་བཅས་པའི་ཉོན་མོངས་པ་ཟད་དེ། གནས་དང་ལུས་དང་ལོངས་སྤྱོད་དུ་སྣང་བའི་རྣམ་པར་རྟོག་པ་རྣམས་སྤངས་པ་ཟག་
པ་མེད་པའི་དབྱིངས་ཀྱང་སྤྲོས་པ་མེད་པ་སྟེ། གསུམ་པོ་འདི་རྣམ་པར་དག་པ་ནམ་མཁའ་ལྟ་བུ་མཐའ་ཡས་པ་སྤྲོས་པ་མེད་པའི་ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྐུ་ཞེས་བྱ་བའི་དོན་ཏོ། །དེའི་རང་བཞིན་དུ་དེའི་ངོ་བོ་ཉིད་དུ་དོན་དམ་དེ་ཡོད་དེ། དེ་བས་དེ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་རང་བཞིན་མངོན་སུམ་དུ་བྱ་བར་དགོངས་སོ། །དེ་ལྟར་ན་དེ་ཉིད་
རྣམ་པར་སྣང་མཛད་དེ་གསལ་བ་ཙམ་དུ་སྣང་བ་དེས་སོ། །དེ་ཉིད་མི་བསྐྱོད་པ་སྟེ་སྣང་བ་མེད་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱིས་སོ། །དེ་ཉིད་དོན་ཡོད་པ་སྟེ་དོན་སྣ་ཚོགས་པ་བྱེད་པས་སོ། །དེ་ཉིད་རིན་པོ་ཆེ་སྟེ། སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཆོས་ཐམས་ཅད་འཐོབ་པས་སོ། །དེ་ཉིད་ཨཱ་རོ་ལྀཀ་སྟེ། དེ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་བདག་ཉིད་
ཡང་དག་པར་སྤྱོད་པས་སོ། །དེ་ལྟར་ཡེ་ཤེས་ལྔའི་རང་བཞིན་དེ་ཉིད་སྙིང་སྟོབས་ཏེ། རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཞེས་བྱ་བའི་དོན་ཏོ། །ཚངས་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ལ། དེ་ཉིད་ཚངས་པ་ལ་སོགས་པར་གསུངས་ཏེ་ཇི་ལྟར་སྙམ་པ་ལ་གསུངས་པ། ཚངས་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པའོ། །གང་དེ་ཉིད་
ཤིན་ཏུ་རྣམ་པར་དག་པ་རྟོགས་པའི་རང་བཞིན་ཏེ། དེ་ཉིད་ཀྱིས་ནི་འདི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཡིན་པས་མཆོག་ཏུ་ཚངས་པ་སྟེ་དེ་བས་ན་ཚངས་པ་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པ་ཞེས་པ་སྟེ་ཐར་པའི་རང་བཞིན་ཉིད་དོ། །མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པ་དང་། ཐར་པ་དང་། ཞི་བ་དང་ཚངས་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནི་རྣམ་གྲངས་སོ། །འཇུག་
པ་ཞེས་པ་ནི་དེའི་བདག་ཉིད་དུ་འཇུག་པས་སོ། །གང་དུ་ཞེ་ན། མཆོག་ཏུ་ཟབ་པ་ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྐུར་རོ། །རྟག་ཏུ་ཤིན་ཏུ་དགེ་བས་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནི་རྟག་ཏུ་དགེ་བའི་ཕྱིར་དང་། མཆོག་ཏུ་དགེ་བའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། །ཐམས་ཅད་ཅེས་བྱ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ལ། གང་གི་ཕྱིར་འདི་ཉིད་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱི་བདག་ཉིད་དུ་ཆོས་ཀྱི་དབྱིངས་
རིག་པར་བྱེད་པ་དེས་གནས་པས་དེའི་ཕྱིར་ཐམས་ཅད་དོ། །མཆོག་གི་བདེ་བ་ཞེས་པ་ནི་ཟག་པ་མེད་པའི་མཆོག་གི་བདེ་བ་བསྟན་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱིས་སོ། །བདེ་བ་རྟོགས་པས་རྣམ་པར་བསད། །ཅེས་པ་ནི་དེ་ཉིད་བླ་ན་མེད་པའི་བདེ་བ་རྟོགས་པ་སྟེ། གང་གིས་དེ་མི་ཤེས་པ་དེ་གཉིད་ལོག་པའོ། །ཚངས་པ་ཞེས་

primordial wisdom, which is the nature of great bliss, is without elaboration because all marks of delusion have subsided. This very perfect primordial wisdom exhausts the afflictions along with their seeds; it is the <term>Dharmakaya</term> which is the unconditioned sphere, free from elaboration, having abandoned the conceptualizations that appear as environment, body, and enjoyments. These three are pure like space, infinite, and the Truth Body without elaboration; such is the meaning. In that nature, as its very essence, that ultimate exists; therefore, the intention is to directly realize its nature. In that way, that very thing is <term>Vairocana</term> <gloss>The Illuminator</gloss>, by appearing as mere clarity. That very thing is <term>Akshobhya</term> <gloss>The Unshakable</gloss>, by its very non-appearance. That very thing is <term>Amoghasiddhi</term> <gloss>Unfailing Accomplishment</gloss>, by performing various purposes. That very thing is <term>Ratnasambhava</term> <gloss>Jewel-Born</gloss>, by obtaining all Buddha-phenomena. That very thing is <term>Arolik</term> <note>Amitabha's family</note>, by perfectly practicing the identity of those. Thus, that very nature of the five wisdoms is the "Being of Heroic Mind" <term>Sattva</term>, which means <term>Vajrasattva</term>. Regarding "Brahma" and so forth: that very thing is spoken of as Brahma and so forth. If one wonders how, it is stated: "Brahma..." and so forth. That which is the very nature of realizing complete purity, by that very fact, this is a Buddha, and thus supreme Brahma; therefore, "Brahma is Nirvana," which is the very nature of liberation. Nirvana, liberation, peace, and Brahma are synonyms. "Entering" means entering as its very identity. Where? Into the profoundly deep <term>Dharmakaya</term>. "By being always perfectly virtuous" is because it is always virtuous and supremely virtuous. Regarding "All..." and so forth: because this very thing cognizes the <term>dharmadhatu</term> as the identity of all, by abiding in that, it is "All." "Supreme Bliss" is by the very showing of the supreme unconditioned bliss. "By realizing bliss, it is killed" means the realization of that very unsurpassed bliss; whoever does not know that is "asleep." Regarding
